gen-dafont-disorder-gf-hind-siliguri: Jagged, raw, and spaced out like it doesn't care. Hind Siliguri follows with a flat, steady hum of line weight, so paragraphs of it settle into a quiet, approachable texture.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-hind-vadodara: Disorder shouts in loose, chaotic letters with oversized lowercase and no swelling at the joins. And Hind Vadodara sits next to it with open, tall-bowled sans shapes, so the two feel like noise and a clean answer.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-huninn: Raw, big-lowercased and scattered, Disorder makes its point loudly. But Huninn keeps its sans letters tidy, with fat crossbars and lowercase near cap height, and shrinking the heading would lose that rough bite.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-inter-tight: Inter Tight bends its lines like tubing, with short ascenders and held-back curve tails. Disorder is best at being loud and raw with its widely spaced, big-lowercase letters, while the sans-serif body is best at staying modern and composed.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-karla: Chunky, tall, and a bit stocky, that's Karla. Disorder is best at rough, widely spaced display shapes with no thin parts, while the plain sans body is best at gaping, approachable openings in a tall middle band.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-kedebideri: Kedebideri reads with a skyward x-height and rounded letters that stay open and inviting, never fussy. The pair's strongest quality is how Disorder's raw, string-steady strokes rub against that friendly sans.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-khula: Neutral is the body's mood, and Khula holds it with a tall midsection and curves that keep their mouths open. Disorder is best at raw, straight-edged, constant strokes, but Khula is best at being a quiet sans-serif underneath.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-krub: Disorder sets chaotic, widely spaced letters whose round walls are as heavy as its straight ones, with oversized lowercase. Krub calms it with a pronounced x-height and unfinished loops.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-kufam: Contemporary in feel, Kufam draws one tube-like track width with open e curves and bodies that dominate the line. The strongest quality is the gap between Disorder's raw scatter and that tidy sans-serif.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-lexend: Disorder looks chaotic and raw, with big lowercase, widely spaced glyphs and no swelling at the joins. Lexend answers with outsized proportions and open jaws on every curve, and its sans stroke thickness holds firm.
